about: Email services recognisable from a domain's own DNS. One block per vendor; imported from dns-audit (MIT) at fac9e2e. Hostname patterns match the host itself or any name under it, and the longest match wins. Every pattern is an entry with its value and a proof: a live domain that publishes it, the record name (or, for a website host, the page) as found, and the date it was checked. Networks are autonomous system numbers a service owns outright; shared clouds are listed under rules.cloud_networks and never credited to a service. Each selectors entry names a vendor's DKIM selectors with their source and a proof; a fixed shape with several names takes a list of proofs, one per name in order. These entries are the only selector list: they credit keys by name, back generic names, and with rules.generic_selectors make the probe sweep. Hints are MX and SPF values the vendor's customers publish, with the pages that list them. Patterns not yet proven wait in vendors_pending.json, which Sendermap never reads.

Amazon SES.selectors_note: No selector entry: Easy DKIM selectors are tokens SES generates per identity, not a series. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/APIReference-V2/API_DkimAttributes.html

Google Workspace.hints_note: The MX page names only smtp.google.com. Domains set up before 2023 use legacy hosts it describes only as starting with aspmx, so those do not match yet.

selectors.note: Not in Mailchimp's own docs. Points at dkim.mcsv.net.
Not in Mailchimp's own docs; reported by third parties. Points at dkim3.mcsv.net.
Customers can choose a custom three character selector, so s1 and s2 are not guaranteed.

SendGrid.hints_note: The docs put these MX and SPF values on the em#### return-path subdomain, not the apex, so an apex scan does not match them.
